extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD contracting officers, procurement staff, and Task Group members involved in A-76/CITA cost-comparison procurements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers and Task Groups conducting A-76 cost-comparison studies and procuring service contracts (C/I support), covering organization, milestone planning, SOW preparation, administration, integrity, and workload/lead-time expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization: customer-oriented contract branches
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regional Contracting Department is organized into customer oriented contracts branches; service-type requests are processed by branches depending on which customer activity submits the purchase request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branches act as single contact points (Branch Supervisor) to facilitate communications with multiple geographically dispersed customers. Cradle-to-grave philosophy is used in some offices; no separate Contract Administration Branch exists in some Navy organizations. Delegation of contract administration to DCAS sometimes occurs and sometimes contract administration is retained by the Procurement Contracting Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation between acquisition and contract administration
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinct differentiation between acquisition and contract administration is desirable (as practiced at Travis AFB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized Services Branch processes service requests; upon award the contract folder is passed to a Contract Administration Branch with formal turnover procedures and requirement that the contract administrator establish a detailed plan for timely contract administration. Almost no contract administration is delegated to DCAS for services in such models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated Contract Administration Branch vs. cradle-to-grave
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider establishing a dedicated Contract Administration Branch rather than retaining cradle-to-grave responsibility with negotiators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cradle-to-grave can enhance continuity but contract administration often slips if negotiators face growing backlogs. Dedicated staff can relieve negotiators and ensure administration/surveillance plans are developed (pre-performance conferences, daily work plans, progress meetings). Feasibility depends on manpower resources and geographic dispersion of supported activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing adequacy and procurement-series billets
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether existing staff and organizations are satisfactory to implement increased contracting effort; most activities indicated understaffing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: levy a requirement on activities engaged in significant contracting-out to establish a procurement-series billet to oversee contract administration and assist in SOW preparation (one person per a given dollar value of contracts). Additional billets likely to appear at the activity receiving the service rather than at contracting offices. Training for these personnel generally must be provided by the contracting office and may itself require additional billets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased requirements for COTRs and QAEs
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs (Contracting Officer's Technical Representatives) and Quality Assurance Evaluators (QAEs) requirements will likely increase as contract administration grows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should plan for additional COTRs/QAEs and ensure these personnel are trained and available to monitor contractor performance; lack of surveillance plans was noted as a common deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT) definition and goal
rubrics_metrics.description: PALT is defined as time from receipt of a purchase request in the contracting office until award of the contract; formal goal for actions over $10,000 (not using simplified purchase) is 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report evidence indicates achieving the 60-day objective will be virtually impossible for many C/I Support Source contract types due to SOW development, solicitation method, auditing, negotiations, and approval delays. Use milestone planning and close monitoring to reduce PALT where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation method impact on lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of solicitation method materially affects procurement lead time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally advertised procedures (including small business restricted advertising) are generally quickest because they avoid technical proposal/cost data submission. Two-Step Formal Advertising requires technical proposals prior to priced bids, lengthening the process. Negotiated procurements including 8(a) set-asides usually take the longest due to required cost/pricing data, audits, and negotiations. Plan solicitation method accordingly when estimating PALT/milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone planning and adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Groups must establish realistic milestones and strive to meet them; milestones drive the duration of the whole A-76/cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestones include preparation of a comprehensive SOW, development of an accurate Government cost estimate, conducting the cost comparison after receipt/evaluation of private sector bids/offers, and preparing the Decision Summary Recommendation for Approving Authority. Contracting Officers should carefully analyze their input to milestone planning to ensure they can perform to the schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer involvement in Task Group planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer should assess his/her level of involvement in the Task Group and be significantly involved early in planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early CO participation benefits milestone planning, SOW development, and maintaining integrity of the competitive bidding system. Reluctance to become involved is common but can result in poorly prepared SOWs unsuitable for solicitation and ill-defined contracting milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group composition and member responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Group typically includes representatives from functional/operational organization, Manpower/Personnel, Finance/Accounting (Comptroller), Legal, and Contracting Office, with a chairperson (often Comptroller or Planning Officer) to lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary responsibilities enumerated: Chairperson (chairs meetings, oversees Government cost estimate, maintains objectivity, sets milestones, guides SOW prep, attends pre-bid/proposal conferences, prepares Decision Summary); Manpower/Personnel (notify unions, identify positions, prepare RIF plans, assist displaced employees); Functional Office (develop SOW, identify GFM, develop Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan); Comptroller/Financial Office (prepare Government cost estimate, conduct cost comparison); Legal Office (review SOW/solicitation for legal sufficiency, assist FOIA responses); Contracting Office (assure milestones met, review specs, solicit bids/offers, conduct pre-bid conferences, preside at bid openings/determine successful responsive/responsible offers, award contracts, notify officials of awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SOW must be written around the same scope of work and level of performance regardless of who performs the work (Government or contractor); responsibility for adequacy rests solely with the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW should be sufficiently precise to avoid misinterpretation, include performance standards that can be monitored for either in-house or contract performance, clearly indicate what is to be done without prescribing how to do it, provide methods of evaluating performance, describe duties/tasks/responsibilities, and specify Government Furnished Material/Facilities/Equipment where necessary. For variable workloads use historical data and best estimates of future requirements. Avoid basing SOWs solely on existing position descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance plan and measurable performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOW and the surveillance plan must be developed together to define desired outcomes, methods of assessing performance, and criteria to determine acceptable or deficient performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A surveillance plan is a key ingredient of a usable SOW; absence of definitive performance standards and surveillance plans was commonly observed and contributed to poor contract administration and difficulty taking action against poor-performing contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the competitive bidding system
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain equitable and consistent treatment of all interested persons and preserve the integrity and objectivity of the competitive bidding system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even the appearance of compromise can lead to severe criticism. The Task Group should emphasize integrity and establish procedures to assure objective treatment. The Chairperson and Contracting Officer have roles in ensuring integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Government in-house cost estimate confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel involved in contracting and evaluation must not have access to the Government in-house cost estimate until the most favorable offer to the Government has been determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the number of personnel with access to the in-house estimate, require Standards of Conduct statements (e.g., per DOD Directive 5500.7), and avoid adjustments to in-house estimates after receipt of offers that could be difficult to justify during audits. Safeguarding cost data is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in cost-comparison and evaluation methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel need familiarization with the technical details of A-76 cost comparison, including methods for evaluating cost-type proposals and incentive arrangements, options handling, and the period over which cost comparisons are based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a four-day Army Logistics Management Center course exists, it may be oriented more to financial management personnel. A dedicated in-house training program based on current guidance is more appropriate. Interviews indicated confusion exists on evaluation methods (e.g., evaluating cost-plus-award-fee proposals), option usage (one-year vs three-year periods), and bid opening procedures for negotiated solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of centralized SOW templates and literature resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Make maximum use of existing centralized SOWs, outlines, and detailed specifications being compiled by Chief of Naval Material and DoD Service Contract Group, and other guidance literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide functional personnel with references such as Base Level Service Contracts, 'Service Contracts, How to Write and Administer Them', and Writing Service Contracts Work Statements to improve SOW quality. Common deficiencies in specifications (e.g., Enclosure (6) to Ref 51) should be distributed to activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award and post-award contractor monitoring procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement pre-performance conferences, daily work plans, periodic progress meetings, and other post-award considerations to surface potential problems early and ensure Government receives contracted services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air Force practice requires scheduling and approval of pre-performance conferences and frequent progress monitoring. Such activities protect Government interests and help monitor QAE/COTR performance in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments, audits, and the 'Adjust Bid/In-House Costs for Comparability' milestone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust bid and in-house costs for comparability, perform necessary audits, and make decisions as a defined milestone in the cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This milestone is acknowledged as somewhat confusing and ill-defined, but it is necessary to ensure comparability between government and private sector offers before final decisions are made. The process may require cost audits and documented adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload impact planning via customer input
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate significant increases in CITA purchase requests by surveying customers and requesting input on probable number/types of functions they will submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As hundreds of functional categories may be reviewed over several years, contracting offices should proactively query customers and use responses as planning aids to allocate resources and set milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer acceptance period management
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should seek longer offer acceptance periods from contractors to mitigate delays and contractor withdrawal risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees suggested extending acceptance periods from the common 60 days to perhaps 75–90 days to avoid loss of key personnel and withdrawal of offers when awards are delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate delays from pre-award surveys, audits, and security/EEO clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award surveys, certification audits, and obtaining security or Equal Employment Opportunity clearances can materially delay contract award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security clearances for contractors can take up to 60 days (interim clearances ~30 days); certification audits and approval process delays (including Congressional bans or policy changes) can extend lead times considerably. Include these factors in milestone/PALT planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of SOW rework and negotiation complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive rework of the SOW or complex negotiations (e.g., with SBA for 8(a) set-asides) can cause lengthy delays and may necessitate resolicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show delays of many months due to SOW rework and SBA negotiations; delayed awards may lead to offer expiration or withdrawal. Contracting Offices should anticipate rework time and plan accordingly.
